lines: A few days ago a legendary entrepreneur said we don't go to the comic book store but if the comics were in the newspaper we'd read them.
This quote genuinely shifted my perspective on how the next generation of millionaires is being made.
Because hear me out, Garfield was free in every newspaper, which is how millions came to recognize it.
They made their billions from selling t-shirts and mugs.
Like the genius Gen Z entrepreneurs are not building comic book stores, they are simply appearing in the newspaper.
The single greatest advantage is existing where all the attention lives, which is social media.
And then building a brand to leverage it, because the thing is nobody goes out of their way for a comic book store, but they won't skip it if it's in their hands.

spine.big_idea: Go where attention already lives and build a brand there, instead of asking people to come to you.
spine.before: I need people to seek out my brand or shop
spine.after: I should show up where people already scroll and monetize later
spine.viewer: Aspiring creators and entrepreneurs building a brand online
spine.format: surprising quote → famous example → what they sold → it's you → principle → brand ask
spine.hook_promise: A quote that changes how you see how new millionaires are made
why: The comic store versus newspaper quote makes you reinterpret it before the lesson lands
Garfield gives a familiar example, so the abstract idea feels concrete
Selling mugs, not comics, shows where the real money is, a quiet twist

points.summary: Show up where attention already lives, then build a brand on it
points.proof: Garfield free in newspapers, then billions from t-shirts and mugs (lines 3-4)

points.summary: People won't seek out your content, but they'll consume what's put in front of them
points.proof: the entrepreneur's comic book store versus newspaper quote (line 1)

points.summary: Social media is today's newspaper, where the attention is
points.proof: Gen Z entrepreneurs appearing in the newspaper, not building stores (line 5)

points.summary: Free distribution builds recognition, and the money comes from the brand
points.proof: Garfield's free newspaper run led to t-shirt and mug billions (lines 3-4)

chunks.wonder: what does comics have to do with making millionaires?
so how did Garfield actually make money?
so what does this mean for people today?
okay, so what do I do with that?

card.name: Attention first
card.use_when: a known example shows people no longer come to you, and I can say where attention is now.
card.needs: a real example people recognise. Missing → don't use this card.
card.reframe: beat 3. The quote or example flips what people assume. Never line 1.

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: Open with a surprising quote or claim that sets up a flip in how people see success.

beats.name: Example
beats.job: Give a familiar example that makes the quote concrete and easy to picture.

beats.name: Reframe
beats.job: Show how the money really came from something other than the obvious product.

beats.name: Why
beats.job: Apply the example to today's builders and say where attention lives now.

beats.name: Payoff
beats.job: End on the one rule: go where people are, then build a brand to use it.

flex: Beat 2 can merge into the hook.
Add a CTA if there is something to offer.
Swap Garfield for any example people know.

said: A famous entrepreneur says people read comics in newspapers, not in comic stores
Garfield spread free through newspapers and reached millions
The billions came from selling t-shirts and mugs, not comics
Gen Z founders appear on social media instead of opening stores
Exist where attention is, then build a brand; nobody seeks out a store
